takeaways: A tour of Highview Park, a new D.R. Horton development in Shakopee near Highways 169 and 101, with about 70 twin home lots plus single-family homes.

With a twin home you own your lot, so you can fence the yard, while the association handles mowing and snow removal. Jason says he hadn't seen new-construction twin homes in the Twin Cities in his 22 years selling.

Prices at the time: the Duet twin home (about 1,650 square feet, four bedrooms upstairs) about $385,000, and the Princeton twin home (about 2,000 square feet, four bedrooms upstairs plus a loft) about $415,000, with a basement option adding about $40,000 to either.

Single-family options: the Henley (five bedrooms, three baths, about 2,600 square feet, around $575,000 to $600,000 depending on options) and the Hulme, a slab-on-grade plan from about $475,000 to $600,000 with a two- or three-car garage. Homes come with smart-home features, sod and landscaping.

faq.q: What is the difference between a twin home and a townhome?
faq.a: With a twin home you typically own the land under your half and your yard, so you can often add a fence. Townhome owners usually own only the unit, with the association owning the land around it. Check each association's rules.

takeaways: Niche ranked Macalester-Groveland the No. 1 neighborhood in Saint Paul. It sits in the southwest part of the city between the Mississippi River bluffs and Summit Avenue, with about 19,700 residents.

It's a true 15-minute neighborhood: groceries (Trader Joe's, Kowalski's), coffee, restaurants and river walks within reach without a car. Downtown Saint Paul and the airport are each about 10 to 15 minutes away, downtown Minneapolis 15 to 20.
Macalester College and the University of St. Thomas are both inside the neighborhood. St. Thomas's new Lee and Penny Anderson Arena (opened October 2025) hosts Division I hockey and basketball.

Tangletown, platted in the late 1800s as part of the Macalester Park addition, has curving streets and homes mostly built from about 1910 to 1940: Craftsman bungalows, American Foursquares and Tudors.
Grand Avenue anchors daily life, with longtime spots like Cafe Latte and W.A. Russell's Bar and Grill in the former Tavern on Grand space. Grand Old Day draws more than 200,000 people.

Early 2026: median in the mid-$400,000s, entry homes from the low $300,000s and larger historic homes from the high $700,000s to about $1 million, typically selling in two to four weeks. The Metro A Line runs along Snelling Avenue.

faq.q: What is the best neighborhood in Saint Paul?
faq.a: Niche ranked Macalester-Groveland No. 1 in Saint Paul, citing its walkability, historic homes, two colleges and access to Grand Avenue and the Mississippi River.

faq.q: How much do homes cost in Macalester-Groveland?
faq.a: In early 2026 the median was in the mid-$400,000s, with entry-level homes from the low $300,000s and larger historic homes up to about $1 million, according to the video.

takeaways: Bloomington and Woodbury are both big, car-oriented suburbs, but they suit different lives.

Location: Bloomington is about 10 miles south of downtown Minneapolis, often about 10 minutes from MSP Airport, and on the Blue Line. Woodbury is about 8 miles east of downtown Saint Paul on I-94, roughly 25 to 30 minutes from the airport.

Prices: Woodbury's median was in the mid-$400,000s (single-family homes in the low $500,000s); Bloomington's mostly in the high $300,000s. Woodbury buys a newer, larger home; Bloomington, an older home in a central spot.

Homes: more than 80% of Bloomington's homes were built from the 1950s to the 1970s, so check the roof, furnace, water heater, windows and sewer line. Woodbury still has active new construction on its east and south edges.

Taxes: Bloomington is in Hennepin County and Woodbury in Washington County. Rates can balance out, but Woodbury's higher prices and possible special assessments in newer neighborhoods matter, so pull the actual tax statement.

Lifestyle: Bloomington has the Mall of America, the Minnesota Valley National Wildlife Refuge and Hyland Lake Park Reserve. Woodbury has 180-plus miles of trails, Carver, Colby and Powers lakes, and is still growing (up about 10% since 2020).

faq.q: Is Bloomington or Woodbury closer to the airport?
faq.a: Bloomington. Many Bloomington homes are about 10 minutes from MSP, while Woodbury is roughly 25 to 30 minutes away, according to the video.

faq.q: Are homes cheaper in Bloomington or Woodbury?
faq.a: Bloomington generally. Its homes were mostly in the high $300,000s versus a mid-$400,000s median in Woodbury, though Woodbury homes tend to be newer and larger.

takeaways: Stillwater calls itself the birthplace of Minnesota: the convention that started the push for statehood met here in the 1840s, and by the 1850s it was a leading lumber town on the St. Croix, before Minneapolis took off.

Downtown sits on the river with neighborhoods climbing the bluffs behind it, connected by historic public staircases. The Lift Bridge is now for walking and biking and forms a loop with the newer St. Croix Crossing bridge.
Well over 100 locally owned shops, restaurants and breweries, including the three-floor Midtown Antique Mall, Lift Bridge Brewing and River Siren, plus sandstone brewery caves in the bluffs.
Outdoors: Brown's Creek State Trail starts downtown and connects to the Gateway Trail toward Saint Paul. The St. Croix is a protected National Scenic Riverway, and there are two full-service marinas.
The trade-off is the commute: about 35 to 40 minutes to downtown Minneapolis in good traffic via Highway 36, longer at rush hour. It works best for remote or hybrid workers.

Prices at the time: entry homes in the low to mid-$400,000s, in-town historic homes from the mid to high $500,000s and bluff-view homes into the low $600,000s. Inventory is tight, and Washington County property taxes run lower than Hennepin or Ramsey.

faq.q: How long is the commute from Stillwater to Minneapolis?
faq.a: About 35 to 40 minutes in good traffic via Highway 36, and longer at rush hour, according to the video.

faq.q: Why is Stillwater called the birthplace of Minnesota?
faq.a: The 1848 convention that started the push for Minnesota's territorial status met in Stillwater, which was also one of the region's earliest lumber towns.

takeaways: The biggest mistake Jason sees: assuming a seller's market means buyers will overlook price. With about 2.5 months of supply the Twin Cities still favor sellers, but inventory is up and buyers check comps and run their payments before they ever book a showing.

Your listing is strongest in its first 7 days, when Zillow, Redfin and Realtor.com push it to the top and send alerts to buyers searching your price range. Price above that range and many of those buyers never see it.
After 3 to 4 weeks without offers, buyers start wondering what's wrong, and a price cut doesn't bring back the ones who've moved on. Homes that sat past 50 days often cut $30,000 to $75,000.
Waiting costs money: Minnesota property taxes rose about 7% this year and homeowners insurance is up close to 40% since 2018, on top of mortgage payments and utilities each month.

Price from recent comps, not a Zestimate or a neighbor's sale from a different market. Updated kitchens and baths, newer mechanicals, professional photos, staging and curb appeal can justify the top of the comp range, but not above it.
Pricing at or just below recent comps creates competition that often pushes the final price at or above asking.

faq.q: Should I price my home at its Zestimate?
faq.a: Jason advises against it. An online estimate hasn't seen your home's updates or condition; price from recent comparable sales and current competition instead.

faq.q: What happens if I overprice my house?
faq.a: It usually sits. After a few weeks buyers start asking what's wrong, price cuts follow, and you pay extra months of mortgage, taxes and insurance, often netting less than if you'd priced right from the start.
